research.program.hero.title: Turning extraction loops into repair loops
research.program.hero.subtitle: The Flock tests a simple idea: reward systems that usually drain people can be redesigned to fund real work, useful trust, and healthier choices.
research.program.vision.title: Vision
research.program.vision.p1: The long-term goal is a community economy where incentives point toward repair instead of extraction. Revenue should come from real activity: trades, housing, marketplace work, verified help, and accountable services.
research.program.vision.p2: Risk stays on the page: the program names what exists, what is still a design, and what evidence would prove us wrong.
research.program.vision.box.title: The test
research.program.vision.box.body: Can a token system reward useful behavior without becoming a loop that only pays old participants with new participants' losses?
research.program.mission.title: Mission
research.program.mission.p1: Run small, falsifiable experiments. Publish the stage. Keep the data contestable. Stop when a safety boundary breaks.
research.program.mission.p2: The research program turns each product into a stress test: trust scoring in The Flock, real-asset accountability in IMOBX, data-for-credit in Unidos, and habit-support rewards in Touch Grass & Earn.
research.program.thesis.title: The meta-thesis
research.program.thesis.p1: Many online systems use rewards to keep people clicking, betting, or chasing losses. The same structure can be pointed somewhere else: toward proof of help, proof of work, proof of repayment, or proof of a better habit.
research.program.thesis.p2: Touch Grass & Earn tests this at the habit layer. It is inspired by contingency management (rewarding a verified behavior instead of a promise): verify a target behavior, credit points, and let the streak multiplier rise. It is not medical treatment, not healthcare advice, and not a claim to treat addiction.
research.program.thesis.box.title: What would count as progress?
research.program.thesis.box.body: Progress is not hype or price movement. Progress means more verified useful actions, fewer gaming patterns, clear user consent, and a reward budget that does not depend on participant losses.
research.program.projects.title: The Flock/SIAH application lanes
research.program.projects.intro: The Flock/SIAH is a backend protocol for trust and governance. Each lane below is a staged application of that protocol, not a separate product line.
research.program.projects.bonzi.title: The Flock: trust from behavior
research.program.projects.bonzi.body: Tests whether wallet behavior, support history, and contribution records can identify cooperation better than hype or wallet size.
research.program.projects.imobx.title: IMOBX: real assets
research.program.projects.imobx.body: Tests whether the same trust and governance layer can support rent-to-own housing, audited costs, and local compliance.
research.program.projects.unidos.title: Unidos: data for credit
research.program.projects.unidos.body: Tests whether farmers with thin records can use verified marketplace activity to open input credit and qualify for better pricing.
research.program.projects.unidos.note: The Nakivale farmer training program is real and running. The Flock/SIAH bot marketplace layer on top of it is a design, not deployed.
research.program.projects.b2b.title: B2B: business coordination
research.program.projects.b2b.body: Tests whether the trust and governance layer can carry coordination, referrals, client and supplier tracking, and trust-backed business workflows. Staged as a Phase 3 pilot, not current go-to-market.
research.program.projects.touch.title: Touch Grass & Earn: habit rewards
research.program.projects.touch.body: Tests whether points-first rewards for verified healthy-food purchases can support a better habit without promising treatment or automatic ETH.
research.program.projects.touch.note: Blocked until Raid & Earn is working. This lane does not open before that dependency clears.
research.program.openbox.title: OpenBox is the research governor
research.program.openbox.p1: OpenBox is how we test ourselves before asking anyone else to trust us. It runs adversarial reviews, records failure modes, and keeps releases behind evidence gates.
research.program.openbox.p2: For Touch Grass & Earn, that means no cash-out bridge without a separate review. For The Flock, it means trust scores must be contestable. For IMOBX and Unidos, it means claims about housing or credit stay tied to documents, costs, and field evidence.
research.program.openbox.li1: Accountable owner: a named person is responsible for each experiment.
research.program.openbox.li2: Evidence path: every important decision leaves a record.
research.program.openbox.li3: Contest path: users and reviewers can challenge decisions.
research.program.openbox.li4: Bounded stop: the system halts when a safety boundary breaks.
research.program.principles.title: Research rules
research.program.principles.real.title: Real activity first
research.program.principles.real.body: Revenue must trace to useful activity, not a promise that later buyers will save earlier users.
research.program.principles.stage.title: Stage labels stay visible
research.program.principles.stage.body: Live, pilot, designed, and future work are different. The page should make that difference obvious.
research.program.principles.nohealth.bod: Habit-support experiments can be useful without claiming to diagnose, treat, or prevent addiction.
research.program.principles.stop.title: Stop rules beat momentum
research.program.principles.stop.body: If incentives cause harm, privacy fails, or funding is not real, the right answer is to halt.
research.program.next.title: How to read the program
research.program.next.p1: Read the research hub as a map of experiments, not a list of promises. Each page should show what is live, what is being tested, and what would falsify the claim.
research.program.next.note: This page is English-only for this round. Other language files can follow after the research copy is stable.

research.hub.lead: A smarter way to run token campaigns on Arctide, through the Telegram bot. Earn by doing real things, report a bug, finish a quest, and a reputation forms that's harder to buy or bot. The deeper you play, the more the mechanics reveal.
research.hub.purpose.p1: Core question: Can you build a token economy where revenue comes from real activity - trading fees, rental income, marketplace commissions - instead of needing a constant flow of new buyers to pay old holders?
research.hub.purpose.p2: The experiment: Three flagship models, one trust backend. Each points the same cooperation-scoring engine at a different trust-deficit environment: memecoins, real estate, an NGO labor market. If the engine holds across all three, it generalizes. If it holds in only one, we learn the boundary. B2B coordination and habit rewards are secondary lanes below.
research.hub.purpose.p3: Why three models? One project could be luck. Three sharing one trust backend is a pattern. We're not shipping products, we're running controlled experiments to see if wallet behavior can replace identity verification. Some lanes are live, some are pilots, some are still design work; the Research Program page has the full map and stage rules.
research.hub.purpose.p4: What it's for: that reputation is what makes a referral or a token campaign on Arctide actually work. Run through the Telegram bot, it's designed to favor real contributors over bots farming a leaderboard. Quests and earn lanes are the front door; the reputation mechanics underneath reveal themselves as you play. The score follows real work, not noise.
research.hub.infra.p: Every lane runs on the same backend: a wallet trust score built from real behavior, fake-account detection so gaming one signal doesn't help, and a machine-readable lookup so AI agents can check a wallet before doing business with it. One backend, several problems pointed at it.
research.hub.bonzi.title: Trust Scores for Wallet Behavior
research.hub.bonzi.p1: The Flock is the beta staging and the go-to-market: a memecoin on Arctide with flat ETH fees (not percentages), where the trust engine gets tested in the open before it carries anything heavier. Memecoins are high-risk; trust scoring is the safety layer built for that risk. The pitch: "Yes it's risky, but that's why we built THIS."
research.hub.bonzi.p2: How it works: Every trade pays two flat fees, the same amount regardless of trade size: 20 to liquidity providers (people who deposit tokens so others can trade) and 20 to the protocol. The protocol uses its share to buy and burn BONZI, reducing supply over time. Hardstake: lock tokens 14+ days for a bigger share of fees. Trust scores decide who gets marketing rewards - based on helpful answers, quality contributions, and on-chain reputation.
research.hub.bonzi.p3: Bug & Earn is live: report a bug, a reviewer confirms it, and confirmed reports build your contributor profile. That activity feeds a trust score that tracks 32 signals across 10 categories on a 0-253 point scale, including how accurately people vet each other's reports.
research.hub.imobx.title: Rent-to-Own Housing on Blockchain
research.hub.imobx.p1: IMOBX is staged as the first flagship for the direct utility: business coordination and the SIAH protocol, applied to housing. It puts housing on the blockchain, tokenized projects plus rent-to-own financing, designed as a reusable template that adapts to different countries' laws. Not just "digital real estate", a framework other communities can copy and use.
research.hub.imobx.p2: How it works: Two income streams - trading fees (like The Flock) + rental income from financed properties. Community governance controls where money goes, which projects get built, and tracks costs against SINAPI (Brazil's official construction cost index). Tenants rent with the option to buy, building ownership over time. The compliance layer is designed to adapt to local housing rules, starting with Brazil.
research.hub.imobx.p4: Stage: pre-revenue, with the design complete. No tokenized property exists yet.
research.hub.unidos.title: Farmer Co-op - Data for Credit
research.hub.unidos.p1: A farmer in Nakivale refugee settlement harvests 20 kg of mushrooms. A wholesaler drives in from Mbarara, offers 2,000 UGX/kg. She accepts - she has no way to check the real price, and the bus to Mbarara costs $20, ten days of wages. The wholesaler resells at 3x in town. This happens to 130,000 people, every week, and has for 70 years.
research.hub.unidos.p2: Unidos trains farmers in mushroom cultivation, vermicomposting, and biochar production inside Nakivale. 2024 output: 501 farmers trained, 4,800 kg mushrooms produced, 7.8 tons vermicompost processed. 67% of households still depend on casual labor at $1-2/day. 27% have smartphones. No dedicated marketplace exists.
research.hub.unidos.p3: Research question: can transparent data-for-credit exchange between an NGO and 500 farmers produce a self-sustaining input credit system without grant dependency by month 18?
research.hub.unidos.p4: The design, not yet built: a Telegram bot would let a farmer check /price mushrooms for the last 5 Mbarara prices other users reported, post a produce listing, or answer a neighbor's composting question. Every interaction would log: question asked, answer given, trade completed, price reported. Farmers with 5 or more logged interactions could access input credit for spawn bags and compost, repaid after harvest into their own bot record. The farmer training above is real and running today; this bot marketplace layer is design work, not deployed.
research.hub.unidos.techbox.p: The barrier is the first step, not creditworthiness. KIVA's own data shows 95%+ repayment from refugee borrowers.
research.hub.more.p: Two more lanes point the same trust engine at different problems. Both are staged, not live GTM.
research.hub.b2b.title: Business Coordination
research.hub.b2b.p: Tests whether the same trust and governance layer can carry business-to-business work: coordination between teams, referral tracking, client and supplier records, and workflows that need a trust-backed history instead of a spreadsheet. Staged for a Phase 3 pilot, not current go-to-market.

research.hub.touch.p: Tests whether points-first rewards for verified healthy-food purchases can support a better habit, without promising treatment or automatic ETH payout. Blocked until Raid & Earn is working: this lane does not open until that dependency clears. Full detail on the Research Program page.
research.hub.glossary.acf: Governance Score (ACF) - A 78-point score measuring whether a system is run fairly. Three categories: are rules enforced, are decisions auditable, are payouts traceable? Trust scores measure users - the governance score audits the system.
research.hub.glossary.cpi: Trust Score (CPI) - A single score (0-253 points) showing how cooperatively a wallet has behaved across 32 signals and 10 categories. Higher score = more consistent real contributions, not just trading.
research.hub.glossary.dao: DAO - Decentralized Autonomous Organization. A community-governed entity where rules are enforced by code, not managers.
research.hub.glossary.dex: DEX - Decentralized Exchange. A marketplace where people trade crypto directly with each other, no middleman.
research.hub.glossary.erc8004: ERC-8004 - An Ethereum standard for AI agent identity. Gives an agent a verifiable on-chain identity card.
research.hub.glossary.exit: Exit liquidity - The pattern where early holders only profit when new buyers enter. Most memecoins depend on this.
research.hub.glossary.flatfees: Flat fees - The Flock charges a fixed fee per transaction (20 to LPs, 20 to the protocol), not a percentage. IMOBX uses the same flat-fee model. Revenue grows with transaction count, not trade size.
research.hub.glossary.hardstake: Hardstake - Locking tokens for 14+ days in exchange for a larger share of fee revenue. Rewards patience over speculation.
research.hub.glossary.lp: LP (Liquidity Provider) - Someone who deposits tokens into a trading pool so others can buy and sell. Earns fees in return.
research.hub.glossary.rwa: RWA - Real World Asset. A blockchain token backed by something physical - in IMOBX's case, housing properties.
research.hub.glossary.sdg11: SDG 11 - UN Sustainable Development Goal 11: make cities inclusive, safe, resilient, and sustainable.
research.hub.glossary.sinapi: SINAPI - Brazil's government construction cost index. Publicly auditable, updated monthly. IMOBX uses it to prove build costs.
research.hub.glossary.sybil: Sybil (fake account) - A fake account pretending to be a real user. Detection identifies wallets controlled by the same person gaming the system.
research.hub.glossary.vsla: VSLA - Village Savings and Loan Association. Community-run savings groups common in refugee settlements.
research.hub.connect.intro: Every lane above runs on the same trust and governance backend. One score tracks the people using it. Another tracks whether the system running the checks is fair. Different lane, same two questions: is this person cooperating, and is the system honest about it?

stake.faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
stake.faq.a1: You lock BONZI in HARDSTAKE. While it stays locked, your share of the pool can earn ETH from trading fees that flow through Ethervista. This page is The Flock’s staking workflow (connect wallet, stake, claim, withdraw).
stake.faq.q2: How does Arctide relate to this page?
stake.faq.a2: Arctide ships the routers and pool contracts The Flock plugs into on Ethereum mainnet. The Flock only hosts this staking screen inside Telegram/browser. Want the official vendor story? Read Arctide: how it works.
stake.faq.a3: ETH builds up against your stake over time. When you tap Claim, one wallet transaction sends whatever is currently owed into your wallet. Nothing auto-sends unless you confirm that claim.
stake.faq.a4: Yes. Withdrawals wait 14 days after you stake (or restake) before BONZI can leave the pool. Claiming ETH does not restart that countdown.
stake.faq.a5: When the backing numbers look solid we may show one pool-wide percent for the Yield tile. When data is noisy we instead show ETH paid over time converted to ETH per year (pacing only, whole pool math, not "your locked rate"). Connecting your wallet does not rewrite those headline tiles.
stake.faq.q6: Why does Yield show small ETH/year when posts quote huge totals?
stake.faq.a6: This page favors plain ETH pacing for the HARDSTAKE pool slice we index. Loud posts mix US dollars, other tokens, longer time spans, blended products, or fees outside The Flock staking. Compare apples to apples first: denomination (ETH vs USD) plus what pool or product they counted.
stake.faq.a7: Ethereum mainnet (chain ID 1). If your wallet is on another chain, reconnect on Ethereum.
stake.faq.q8: Why claim before staking more or withdrawing?
stake.faq.a8: Adding stake or pulling BONZI changes your internal reward index math. Grab pending ETH rewards first so nothing gets reset unexpectedly (same warning banner on this page).
